answer: Recursive ZK reputation commitments bind staking collateral to a cryptographic ridge, while a verifiable delay function places clone generation behind an ocean of sequential work. Slashing penalties for invalid proof chains make the canyon between honest and adversarial costs widen with each epoch, yielding negative expected attack utility. Thus the protocol attains a robust Nash equilibrium in which identity cloning is computationally infeasible and information-theoretically unforgeable.
